paragraphs: Valaris Limited is a global offshore contract drilling company. Unless the context requires otherwise, the terms "Valaris," "Company," "we," "us" and "our" refer to Valaris Limited together with all its subsidiaries and predecessors.

We are a leading provider of offshore contract drilling services to the international oil and gas industry with operations in almost every major offshore market across six continents. Our fleet of offshore drilling rigs is among the largest in the world and includes one of the highest specification ultra-deepwater fleets, as well as a leading premium jackup fleet. As of February 20, 2026, we own 46 rigs, including 13 drillships, two semisubmersible rigs, 31 jackup rigs and a 50% equity interest in ARO, our 50/50 unconsolidated joint venture with Saudi Aramco, which owns an additional nine rigs.

Our customers include many of the leading international and government-owned oil and gas companies, in addition to many independent operators. We are among the most geographically diverse offshore drilling companies with global operations. The markets in which we operate include the Gulf of America, South America, the North Sea, the Mediterranean, the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific.

We provide drilling services on a day rate contract basis. Under day rate contracts, we provide an integrated drilling service that includes the provision of a drilling rig and rig crews for which we receive a daily rate that may vary between the full rate and zero rate throughout the duration of the contractual term, depending on the operations of the rig. We also may receive lump-sum fees or similar compensation for the mobilization, demobilization and capital upgrades of our rigs. Our customers bear substantially all of the costs of constructing the well and supporting drilling operations as well as the economic risk relative to the success of the well.
Pending Business Combination with Transocean

On February 9, 2026, Valaris and Transocean Ltd. ("Transocean") entered into a business combination agreement (the "Business Combination Agreement") under which Transocean will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for shares of Transocean at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share. The Business Combination will be effected by way of a court-approved scheme of arrangement between Valaris and the holders of the Valaris shares pursuant to section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda, as amended. The Transocean shares are expected to be issued in reliance on the exemption from the registration requirements of the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended, provided by Section 3(a)(10) thereof and pursuant to exemptions from registration under any applicable state securities laws. Following the consummation of the Business Combination, Transocean's existing shareholders and Valaris' existing shareholders will own approximately 53% and 47%, respectively, of the combined company on a fully diluted basis assuming conversion to shares of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029. See "Part II. Item 7 - Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations - Introduction - Pending Business Combination with Transocean" for further information.

The offshore drilling industry is cyclical and primarily influenced by global energy demand, oil and gas supply dynamics and customer capital allocation decisions. Periods of oil oversupply generally place downward pressure on commodity prices, while periods of undersupply can result in higher and more volatile oil prices, influencing investment decisions across the upstream sector. While the oil market is currently in a period of oversupply, industry fundamentals are generally viewed as constructive over the medium to long term. Market participants generally expect the current oil supply imbalance to shift to a structurally tighter market over the next few years, driven by past underinvestment in upstream development and slowing production growth from non-OPEC sources. Industry studies, including those published by the International Energy Agency and the U.S. Energy Information Administration, indicate that substantial upstream investment is required to offset natural field declines and maintain existing production levels.

Against this backdrop, customers continue to emphasize the need for sustained investment in oil and gas to support secure, reliable and affordable energy supply, with increasing focus on offshore developments, particularly in deepwater. Compared to other sources of supply, deepwater projects typically offer large resource potential, competitive project economics and lower carbon intensity per barrel. Despite near-term commodity price uncertainty, customers are continuing to advance long-cycle offshore developments. Industry participants anticipate increased deepwater project sanctioning over the next five years across greenfield, brownfield and exploration opportunities. According to Rystad Energy estimates, approximately 70% of this expected activity is associated with projects with breakeven oil prices below $50 per barrel and over 80% is associated with projects with breakeven prices below $60 per barrel.

Operating results in the offshore drilling industry are directly related to the demand for and the available supply of drilling rigs, each of which affects rig utilization and day rates. While the balance of rig supply and demand can vary somewhat between regions, significant variations between most regions are generally short-term due to rig mobility. Rig attrition in the industry over the last decade, particularly for floaters, has resulted in a smaller global fleet of rigs that is available to meet customer demand.

Our business consists of four operating segments: (1) Floaters, which includes our drillships and semisubmersible rigs, (2) Jackups, (3) ARO and (4) Other, which consists of management services on rigs owned by third parties and the activities associated with our lease arrangements with ARO. Floaters, Jackups and ARO are also reportable segments.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned 46 rigs and excluding our held-for-sale rig, 17 are located in Europe, 16 are located in Middle East and Africa, eight are located in North and South America and four are located in Asia and the Pacific Rim.

Our drilling rigs drill and complete oil and natural gas wells. From time to time, our drilling rigs may be utilized as accommodation units or for other ancillary services such as well workovers and interventions, plug and abandonment and decommissioning work and carbon capture and sequestration projects. Demand for our drilling services is based upon many factors beyond our control. See "Item 1A. Risk Factors - The success of our business depends on the level of activity in offshore oil and natural gas exploration, which can be significantly affected by volatile oil and natural gas prices."

headings: Risks Related to the Business Combination
While the Business Combination Agreement is in effect, we are subject to restrictions on our business activities.
Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, Financing Arrangements and Market Conditions

The success of our business depends on the level of activity in offshore oil and natural gas exploration, development and production, which can be significantly affected by volatile oil and natural gas prices.
The offshore contract drilling industry is highly competitive and cyclical.
Our current backlog of contract drilling revenue may not be fully realized and may decline significantly in the future.
Our business will be materially adversely affected if we are unable to secure contracts on economically favorable terms or if option periods in existing contracts are not exercised as expected.
Our customers may be unable or unwilling to fulfill their contractual commitments to us, including their obligations to pay for losses, damages or other liabilities.
The loss of a significant customer or customer contract, as well as customer consolidation and changes to customer strategy, could materially adversely affect our business.
Our long-term contracts are subject to the risk of cost increases, which could adversely impact our profitability.
Our network and systems, including rig operating systems and critical data, are subject to cybersecurity risk and technical disruptions.

Rig reactivation, upgrade and enhancement projects are subject to risks, including delays and cost overruns, which could materially adversely affect our financial position, operating results or cash flows.
Failure to recruit, develop and retain skilled personnel could materially adversely affect our business.
AI presents risks and challenges that can impact our business.
We may not realize the expected benefits of our ARO joint venture.
Joint venture investments could be adversely affected by our joint venture partners' actions, financial condition and liquidity and disputes between us and our joint venture partners.
Our business involves operating hazards, and our insurance and indemnities from our customers or other parties may not be adequate to cover any potential losses.
Geopolitical events and violence could materially adversely affect the markets for our services and have a material adverse effect on our business and cost and availability of insurance.
Our drilling contracts with national oil companies may expose us to greater risks than we normally assume in drilling contracts with non-governmental customers.
Unionization efforts and labor regulations in certain countries in which we operate could materially increase our costs or limit our flexibility with regard to the management of our personnel.
paragraphs: Our pending Business Combination may be delayed or not occur at all for a variety of reasons, some of which are outside of the parties' control, and if these conditions are not satisfied, the Business Combination Agreement may be terminated and the Business Combination may not be completed.

On February 9, 2026, Valaris and Transocean (Valaris and Transocean, collectively, the "Parties" and each, a "Party"), entered into a business combination agreement (the "Business Combination Agreement"), providing for the combination of the two Parties (the "Business Combination"). Pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement, and on the terms and subject to the conditions thereof, Transocean will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for shares of Transocean at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share. The Business Combination will be effected by way of a court-approved scheme of arrangement between Valaris and the holders of the Valaris shares pursuant to section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda, as amended. Following the consummation of the Business Combination, Transocean's existing shareholders and Valaris' existing shareholders will own approximately 53% and 47%, respectively, of the combined company on a fully diluted basis assuming conversion to shares of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029.

Completion of the Business Combination is subject to customary closing conditions, including (1) the receipt of the requisite approvals of the Valaris shareholders and the Transocean shareholders, (2) the granting of the sanction order on terms consistent with the Business Combination Agreement, (3) the Transocean shares issued pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement having been approved for listing on the NYSE, (4) certain regulatory approvals having been obtained or any applicable waiting period having expired or been terminated, (5) no governmental authority within applicable jurisdictions having enacted or issued any law or order preventing or prohibiting the consummation of the Business Combination and (6) the absence of a Transocean Material Adverse Effect or a Valaris Material Adverse Effect (as each are defined in the Business Combination Agreement). Therefore, the Business Combination Agreement may not be completed or may not be completed as timely as expected.

In addition, the Business Combination Agreement also contains certain customary termination rights in favor of each Party, including for the failure to receive the requisite approvals of the Valaris shareholders and Transocean shareholders. A Party may terminate the Business Combination Agreement, prior to the receipt of the requisite approval of the other Party's shareholders, if the other Party shall have made an Adverse Recommendation Change (as defined in the Business Combination Agreement). Either Valaris or Transocean may terminate the Business Combination Agreement if the effective time shall not have occurred on or prior to February 9, 2027 (as such date may be extended in accordance with the terms of the Business Combination Agreement).
Failure to complete the Business Combination could adversely affect our business and the market price of our common shares in a number of ways, including:

paragraphs: Valaris Limited 為一間全球性離岸合同鑽井公司。除非上下文另有要求，否則 "Valaris"、"Company"、"we"、"us" 及 "our" 皆指 Valaris Limited 連同其所有子公司及前身。

我們是國際油氣產業離岸合同鑽井服務的主要提供者，業務遍及六大洲幾乎所有主要離岸市場。我們的離岸鑽井 rigs 羣是全球規模最大的之一，包含其中規格最高的超深水 rigs 羣，以及領先的高階 jackup rigs 羣。截至 2026 年 2 月 20 日，我們擁有 46 臺 rigs，包括 13 臺 drillships、2 臺 semisubmersible rigs、31 臺 jackup rigs，以及在 ARO 的 50% 股權，此為我們與沙特阿拉伯國家油公司（Saudi Aramco）共同成立的 50/50 未合併聯營公司，擁有額外 9 臺 rigs。
我們的客戶包括許多國際領先及國有油氣公司，以及許多獨立經營者。我們是地理分佈最廣的離岸鑽井公司之一，擁有全球性業務。我們經營的市場包括美洲 Gulf of Mexico、南美洲、北海、地中海、中東、非洲及亞太地區。
我們以每日費用合約方式提供鑽井服務。根據每日費用合約，我們提供整合式鑽井服務，包括提供鑽井 rigs 及 rigs 人員，我們會根據合約期間 rigs 的運作情況，收取每日費用，該費用可能在合約期間內介於全額費用與零費用之間。我們也可能會因 rigs 的調動、解調及資本升級而收取一次性費用或類似報酬。我們的客戶承擔構建井及支援鑽井作業的幾乎所有成本，以及與井的成功率相關的經濟風險。
待完成之企業併購與 Transocean

2026 年 2 月 9 日，Valaris 與 Transocean Ltd.（"Transocean"）簽訂企業併購協議（"Business Combination Agreement"），根據協議，Transocean 將以 Transocean 股票換取 Valaris 所有已發行及流通的普通股，交換比例為每 1 股 Valaris 股票換取 15.235 股 Transocean 股票。此企業併購將透過一項由法院批准的安排方案（scheme of arrangement）進行，該方案根據百慕達 1981 年公司法（Companies Act 1981）及其修正案第 99 節進行。Transocean 股票預期將根據美國 1933 年證券法（Securities Act of 1933）及其修正案第 3(a)(10) 節所提供的免於註冊要求豁免，以及根據任何適用州證券法的註冊豁免而發行。企業併購完成後，Transocean 現有股東與 Valaris 現有股東將分別持有合併後公司約 53% 及 47% 的股份，假設轉換為 Transocean 2029 年可轉換債券。請參閱 "Part II. Item 7 - 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析 - 簡介 - 待完成之企業併購與 Transocean" 以取得更多資訊。

離岸鑽井產業為週期性產業，主要受全球能源需求、油氣供應動態及客戶資本配置決策影響。油價過度供應的時期通常會對商品價格造成向下壓力，而供應不足的時期則可能導致油價更高且更波動，影響上游產業的投資決策。雖然目前油價處於過度供應時期，但產業基本面普遍被視為中長期正面。市場參與者普遍預期，目前的油價供應失衡將在未來幾年轉變為結構性緊縮的市場，這是由過去上游開發投資不足及非 OPEC 來源生產增長放緩所驅動。產業研究，包括國際能源機構（International Energy Agency）及美國能源資訊管理局（U.S. Energy Information Administration）所發表的研究，指出需要大量上游投資以抵消自然油田衰退並維持現有生產水平。

在這種背景下，客戶持續強調需要持續投資於油氣產業以支持安全、可靠且可負擔的能源供應，並日益關注離岸開發，特別是在深水區。與其他供應來源相比，深水區項目通常具有巨大的資源潛力、競爭性的項目經濟效益及較低的每桶碳強度。儘管近期商品價格不確定性，客戶仍持續推進長期週期的離岸開發。產業參與者預期未來五年內將增加深水區項目的核准，涵蓋綠地、棕地及勘探機會。根據 Rystad Energy 的估計，約 70% 的預期活動與 breakeven 油價低於每桶 50 美元的項目相關，超過 80% 的預期活動與 breakeven 油價低於每桶 60 美元的項目相關。
營運成果在離岸鑽井產業中與鑽井 rigs 的需求及供應直接相關，每者皆會影響 rigs 的使用率及日租率。雖然 rigs 的供應與需求平衡在不同地區可能略有差異，但大多數地區之間的重大差異通常是短期的，因為 rigs 可移動性較高。過去十年間，產業中 rigs 的折舊，特別是對於 floaters，導致可用以應對客戶需求的全球 rigs 數量減少。
本公司業務包含四個營運分部：(1) Floaters，包含本公司所有之鑽探船及半潛式 rigs，(2) Jackups，(3) ARO，以及(4) 其他，包含為第三方所有 rigs 提供管理服務，以及與 ARO 之租約活動。Floaters、Jackups 及 ARO 亦為應報告分部。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有 46 臺 rigs，扣除待出售 rigs 後，17 臺位於歐洲，16 臺位於中東及非洲，8 臺位於北美洲及南美洲，4 臺位於亞洲及太平洋沿岸。
本公司之鑽井 rigs 用以鑽探及完成石油及天然氣井。有時本公司之鑽井 rigs 可用作住宿單位，或用於其他輔助服務，例如井的維修及幹擾、封井及棄置工作，以及碳捕捉及封存計畫。本公司鑽井服務之需求取決於許多超出本公司控制範疇的因素。請參閱「第 1A 項 風險因素 - 本公司業務之成功取決於離岸石油及天然氣探勘活動之程度，而此活動可能因石油及天然氣價格波動而受到顯著影響。」

paragraphs: 下列資訊應與「第 1A 項 風險因素」及我們的合併財務報表與相關附註，即「第 8 項 財務報表與補充資料」一併閱讀。
本節對我們營運成果與流動性的討論包含 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度的比較。如需類似討論，包括 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財務年度的比較，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度的 10-K 年度報告，於 2025 年 2 月 20 日提交至 SEC。

我們是國際油氣產業 offshore 合約鑽井服務的主要供應商，業務遍及六大洲幾乎所有主要 offshore 市場。我們的 offshore 鑽井 rigs 羣是全球規模最大的之一，包含其中規格最高的 ultra-deepwater 鑽井 rigs，以及領先的 premium jackup 鑽井 rigs。截至 2026 年 2 月 20 日，我們擁有 46 臺 rigs，包括 13 臺 drillships、2 臺 semisubmersible rigs、31 臺 jackup rigs，以及在 ARO 的 50% 股權，這是我們與 Saudi Aramco 合資的 50/50 未合併聯營公司，擁有額外 9 臺 rigs。
我們的客戶包括許多國際及政府所有的油氣公司，以及許多獨立經營者。我們是全球業務範圍最廣的 offshore 鑽井公司之一。我們營運的市場包括美洲 Gulf of Mexico、南美洲、北海、地中海、中東、非洲與亞太地區。
我們以每日費用合約方式提供鑽井服務。根據每日費用合約，我們提供整合式鑽井服務，包含提供鑽井 rigs 與 rigs 人員，我們根據合約期間內 rigs 的運作情況，收取每日費用，該費用可能在全額費用與零費用之間變動。我們也可能因 rigs 的動員、解體與資本升級而收取一次性費用或類似報酬。我們的客戶承擔構建井與支援鑽井作業的大部分成本，以及與井的成功率相關的經濟風險。

offshore 鑽井產業具有週期性，主要受全球能源需求、油氣供應動態與客戶資本配置決策影響。油價過度供應的時期通常對商品價格產生向下壓力，而供應不足的時期則可能導致油價更高且更波動，影響上游產業的投資決策。雖然目前油價處於過度供應時期，但產業基本面普遍被視為中長期正面。市場參與者普遍預期目前的油價供應失衡將在未來幾年轉變為結構性緊縮市場，這是由過去上游開發投資不足與非 OPEC 來源生產增長放緩所驅動。

在這種背景下，客戶持續強調需要持續投資於油氣產業，以支持安全、可靠且可負擔的能源供應，並日益關注 offshore 開發，特別是在深水區。與其他供應來源相比，深水區項目通常具有巨大的資源潛力、競爭性的項目經濟效益與較低的每桶碳強度。儘管近期商品價格不確定性，客戶仍持續推動長週期的 offshore 開發。產業參與者預期未來五年內，將增加深水區項目核准，涵蓋綠地、棕地與勘探機會。根據 Rystad Energy 的估計，約 70% 的預期活動與 breakeven 油價低於每桶 50 美元的項目相關，超過 80% 的項目與 breakeven 油價低於每桶 60 美元的項目相關。
offshore 鑽井產業的營運成果直接與鑽井 rigs 的需求與供應有關，這兩者均影響 rigs 的使用率與每日費用。雖然不同地區的 rigs 供應與需求平衡可能略有不同，但大多數地區之間的顯著差異通常是短期的，因為 rigs 的移動性較高。過去十年間產業中 rigs 的折舊，特別是 floaters，導致可用於滿足客戶需求的全球 rigs 數量減少。
通貨膨脹壓力影響我們的成本基礎，導致人力成本增加，以及我們操作鑽井 rigs 或執行資本計畫所需商品與服務的價格上漲。此外，美元對外幣的貶值可能使我們在某些外國司法管轄區的營運成本增加。我們預期在近期內成本將持續上升，特別是考慮到增加的關稅對全球貿易的潛在影響，儘管我們部分長期合約包含成本上漲的條款，我們無法確定我們能否成功向客戶聲請補償更高的成本，根據這些契約條款。

2026 年 2 月 9 日，Valaris 與 Transocean（Valaris 與 Transocean 合稱「當事人」，各為「當事人」），簽訂一項企業合併協議，根據該協議，Transocean 將取得 Valaris 全部已發行且流通的普通股，以 Transocean 股票交換，交換比率為每 1 股 Valaris 股票換取 15.235 股 Transocean 股票。此企業合併將透過一項經法院批准的安排方案（scheme of arrangement）進行，根據伯明翰 1981 年公司法（Companies Act 1981）第 99 條，該法已修正。Transocean 股票預期將根據 1933 年美國證券法（Securities Act of 1933）第 3(a)(10) 條所提供的註冊要求豁免，以及根據任何適用州證券法的註冊豁免而發行。企業合併完成後，Transocean 現有股東與 Valaris 現有股東將持有約 53% 與 47% 的合併後公司股份，以完全稀釋後的基礎計算，假設轉換為 Transocean 2029 年可轉換債券的股份。

企業合併的完成需符合慣常的交割條件，包括（1）Valaris 股東與 Transocean 股東的必要批准，（2）制裁令在符合企業合併協議條款的條件下獲得，（3）根據企業合併協議發行的 Transocean 股票已獲 NYSE 上市批准，（4）已獲得某些監管批准或任何適用的等待期已過期或終止，（5）任何適用司法管轄區的政府機構未頒布或發佈任何法律或命令阻止或禁止企業合併的完成，以及（6）不存在 Transocean 重大不利影響或 Valaris 重大不利影響。因此，企業合併協議可能無法完成，或可能無法按預期時間完成。

此外，企業合併協議也包含某些慣常的終止權，有利於每一當事人，包括因未能獲得 Valaris 股東與 Transocean 股東的必要批准。此外，一當事人可在未獲得另一當事人股東必要批准前，終止企業合併協議，如果另一當事人已作出不利建議變更（如企業合併協議所定義）。此外，Valaris 或 Transocean 可以在 2027 年 2 月 9 日（如根據企業合併協議條款可延長）前，終止企業合併協議，若有效時間未發生。若根據特定情況終止企業合併協議，包括若 Valaris 因 Transocean 作出不利建議變更（如企業合併協議所定義）而終止企業合併協議，或因其他特定觸發事件，Valaris 將需向 Transocean 支付 1.73 億美元的終止費用。
上述企業合併協議及預期交易的描述並非完整，且完全以參考企業合併協議為準，該協議副本已作為 8-K 現行報告的附錄 2.1 註冊，於 2026 年 2 月 10 日提交至 SEC。
請參閱「第一部分 第 1A 項 - 風險因素」以進一步討論與企業合併相關的風險。

與本公司業務、營運、融資安排及市場條件相關之風險
本公司業務之成功取決於離岸石油及天然氣探勘、開發及生產之活躍程度，而此等活躍程度可能因油氣價格波動而顯著影響。
離岸合同鑽井產業具有高度競爭性且具週期性。
本公司目前合同鑽井收入之待執行訂單可能無法完全實現，且未來可能顯著減少。
若本公司無法以經濟上有利之條款取得合同，或現有合同中選項期間未如預期執行，將對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司客戶可能無法或不願履行對本公司之契約義務，包括其支付損失、損害或其他責任之義務。
失去重要客戶或客戶契約，以及客戶整併與客戶策略變更，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司長期契約面臨成本上升的風險，可能對本公司利潤率造成不利影響。
本公司網路與系統，包括鑽井平台作業系統與關鍵資料，面臨網路安全風險與技術中斷的風險。
鑽井平台重新啟動、升級與增強專案面臨風險，包括延誤與成本超支，可能對本公司財務狀況、營運成果或現金流造成重大不利影響。
未能招募、培訓與留住具專業技能的人員，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
人工智慧（AI）帶來風險與挑戰，可能影響本公司業務。
本公司可能無法實現與ARO合資公司的預期效益。
合資公司投資可能因合資夥伴的行為、財務狀況與流動性及雙方之間的爭議而受到不利影響。
本公司業務涉及操作風險，且本公司自客戶或其他當事人取得的保險及賠償可能不足以彌補任何潛在損失。
國際政治事件及暴力行為可能對本公司服務的市場造成重大不利影響，並對本公司業務及保險的費用與可取得性產生重大不利影響。
本公司與國家油公司簽訂的鑽井合約，可能使本公司面臨較一般非政府客戶鑽井合約中所承擔的風險更高的情況。
本公司在某些營運國家所面臨的工會化運動及勞動法規，可能導致本公司成本大幅增加或限制本公司在管理員工方面之彈性。
paragraphs: 本公司待決之企業併購可能因多種原因而延遲或完全無法進行，部分原因在於各當事人之控制範圍之外，若這些條件未達成，企業併購協議可能終止，企業併購可能無法完成。

2026年2月9日，Valaris與Transocean（Valaris與Transocean合稱為「當事人」，各為「當事人」），簽訂企業併購協議（「企業併購協議」），規範兩當事人之結合（「企業併購」）。根據企業併購協議，並依協議條款及條件，Transocean將以15.235股Transocean股份兌換每一股Valaris股份，換取Valaris所有已發行且流通之普通股。企業併購將透過一項經法院批准之安排方案進行，該安排方案係根據伯明翰公司法1981年版（已修正）第99條之規定，由Valaris與Valaris股份持有人之間進行。企業併購完成後，Transocean現有股東與Valaris現有股東將分別持有合併後公司約53%與47%之股份，此為假設轉換為Transocean可轉換債券（2029年到期）之股份後之情況。

企業併購之完成須符合慣例性關閉條件，包括（1）Valaris股東與Transocean股東取得必要批准、（2）根據企業併購協議之條款取得制裁令、（3）根據企業併購協議發行之Transocean股份已獲批准於紐約證券交易所上市、（4）已取得某些監管批准或任何適用之等待期已屆滿或終止、（5）任何適用司法管轄區之政府機關未頒布或發佈任何法律或命令阻止或禁止企業併購之完成，以及（6）不存在Transocean重大不利影響或Valaris重大不利影響（如各項所定義於企業併購協議中）。因此，企業併購協議可能無法完成，或可能無法如期完成。
此外，企業併購協議亦包含若干慣例性終止權，有利於各當事人，包括因未能取得Valaris股東與Transocean股東之必要批准。若另一當事人已作出不利建議變更（如企業併購協議所定義），則任一當事人可在未取得另一當事人股東之必要批准前終止企業併購協議。若有效時間未於2027年2月9日或之前發生（如企業併購協議條款所允許之延長），則Valaris或Transocean可終止企業併購協議。
未能完成企業併購可能以多種方式對本公司業務及本公司普通股之市場價格產生不利影響，包括：
•本公司普通股之市場價格可能下跌，因目前市場價格可能基於企業併購將完成之假設。
